label: Core Concepts
desc: 15 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Freshness, Validation, Checks and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: What does data quality mean in data engineering? What are common dimensions of data quality?

subs.label: Freshness
subs.desc: Freshness is how recently data was updated relative to expected cadence.

subs.label: Validation
subs.desc: Validation checks whether a dataset satisfies rules (types, constraints, ranges).

subs.label: Checks
subs.desc: What are row-level checks and aggregate checks? What is the minimum set of checks you would add to every table?

subs.label: Pipelines
subs.desc: How do you design quality checks for incremental pipelines? How do you handle late arriving data from a quality perspective?

subs.label: Schema
subs.desc: How do you detect schema drift and breaking changes?

subs.label: Contracts
subs.desc: Data contracts are explicit agreements between producers and consumers about schema, semantics, SLAs, and ownership.

subs.label: Alerting
subs.desc: How do you avoid noisy alerts (false positives) in data quality monitoring?

subs.label: Monitoring
subs.desc: What is anomaly detection for metrics and when is it useful?

subs.label: Testing
subs.desc: How do you test data transformations?

subs.label: Failure Modes
subs.desc: What are common data quality failure modes?

subs.label: Tooling
subs.desc: Great Expectations is a Python framework for defining data quality rules ("expectations" — expect_column_values_to_not_be_null, expect_column_values_to_be_between) as declarative, version-controllable code rather than one-off SQL scripts.

subs.label: Profiling
subs.desc: Profiling means computing summary statistics on a dataset before you know what to check — null rates per column, distinct value counts, min/max/mean, common patterns in string columns.

label: Practical Validation Techniques
desc: 6 interview questions covering Referential Integrity, Deduplication, Statistical Checks, Streaming and more.

subs.label: Referential Integrity
subs.desc: Most analytical warehouses accept (but don't enforce) foreign key declarations, so referential integrity has to be checked explicitly — typically an anti-join: rows in the child table whose key doesn't exist in the parent table.

subs.label: Deduplication
subs.desc: What techniques do you use to detect duplicate records at scale?

subs.label: Statistical Checks
subs.desc: How do you detect distribution drift in a column's values over time?

subs.label: Streaming
subs.desc: Batch checks run against a complete, stable dataset; streaming checks have to work against data that's still arriving, with no natural "batch is done" moment to validate against.

subs.label: Data Modeling
subs.desc: How do you decide between NULL, an empty string, and a sentinel value for missing data?

subs.label: Pipeline Design
subs.desc: Light structural checks (can it be parsed, does it match the expected raw schema) belong at bronze, right on ingestion, so malformed source data is caught immediately rather than propagating.

label: Metrics, Ownership & Trust
desc: 4 interview questions covering Metrics, Prioritization, Ownership, Trust.

subs.label: Metrics
subs.desc: How do you build a data quality score, and what would it be based on?

subs.label: Prioritization
subs.desc: How do you decide how much quality investment a dataset actually needs?

subs.label: Ownership
subs.desc: Who should own a data quality failure — the producing team or the consuming team?

subs.label: Trust
subs.desc: Be transparent about what happened and why, rather than quietly fixing it — a short incident writeup (what broke, what was affected, what's changing) does more for trust than silence.
